o.text: Borrowed from Persian چهرهای (čehre-'i, literally “facial”), from چهره (čehre, “face”), because the completion of skin gives off pink undertones. Compare Southern Azerbaijani صؤرتی (sürəti), from Persian صورت (surat, “face”). By surface analysis, çöhrə + -i.
Borrowed from Arabic أَهَالِي (ʔahālī), the informal pronunciation of أَهَالٍ (ʔahālin), plural of أَهْل (ʔahl).
Borrowed from Classical Persian اهل معرفت (ahl-i ma'rifat).
From Arabic ظَرَافَة (ẓarāfa). Doublet of zərafət.
From Proto-Turkic *ger- (“to spread out, to hang”). Cognate with Turkish germek, Chuvash кар (kar), etc.
From Persian اژگهان (ažgahân), in some dialects possibly via Tat.
From göt + -əş. The function of the suffix is unclear here.
